entry_state: A written put caps the retained asset and a collar subtracts the full put value. Amortised-cost transfers need separate asset and liability yields; the common transfer does not justify one shared rate.
exit_state: Facility capacity, requests and actual receipts are distinct. Missing acknowledgement preserves alternative settlement histories; supported cash must be recorded even after a control violation. Accounting, prudential assessment and behavioural policy retain separate evidence. The review now turns to insurance service, finance and claims.
findings: The funding cases have confirmed borrowing 8, 6 or 0 and unpaid obligations 2, 4 or 10. All end with equity 20, so equity alone cannot identify liquidity failure severity.
Unpaid deposits stay inside the liability rather than being added again. A request creates no cash, and timeout alone does not prove no receipt.
The final prudential example labels deduction and RWA as synthetic; bank-specific applicability and behavioural calibration remain separate. No new defect observed.
